Mechanics: Make sure all forces are accounted for in the system, including friction and normal forces.
Avoid assuming uniform motion without verifying the net force acting on the object.
Check that energy conversions are correctly identified and conserved across all forms.
Thermodynamics: Make sure all materials involved have known specific heat capacities and thermal properties.
Avoid assuming equilibrium temperature without considering heat transfer rates and thermal isolation.
Check that all temperature conversions are consistent and use absolute scales where necessary.
Biology: Make sure all forces and torques are accounted for in the forearm problem.
Avoid assuming uniformity in genetic inheritance without proper evidence.
Check that the devised mass measurement scheme accounts for inertia and acceleration.
Chemistry: Make sure all reactions are balanced and stoichiometric relationships are correctly applied.
Avoid mixing different solution concentrations without proper conversion between units.
Check that all given data is consistent with the laws of conservation and thermodynamic principles.
Electromagnetism: Make sure all quantities are in consistent units before calculations. Avoid mixing different unit systems.
Avoid assuming symmetry or simplifications without justification. Check if all given data is relevant.
Ensure that induced effects like emf or current are properly linked to changing fields or currents. Avoid missing dependencies.
Optics: Make sure all materials involved have known and consistent refractive indices.
Avoid combining different optical phenomena unless their interactions are well understood.
Check that all given angles are measured from the normal unless stated otherwise.
Materials Science: Make sure the problem clearly defines the material properties and their relevance to the design question.
Avoid combining unrelated scientific domains without a clear integrative context.
Check that all quantitative aspects are grounded in established material science principles.
Energy Systems: Make sure all energy units are consistent across the problem.
Avoid combining unrelated energy systems without clear context.
Check that conservation laws are properly applied in all scenarios.
